regime.skew: balanced (+0.17) — the 25D put bid is fully paid down, abnormal for an index
regime.label: Dealer short gamma for an 8th session but the amplifier halved: the future rose 9.2 points while upside call IV was crushed 2.1 points and the 1070 call wing was closed out
evidence: -3,817 net GEX (gamma x OI x 200) across the 950-1150 grid versus -7,476 yesterday — the short-gamma burden halved in one session; cumulative net GEX is negative at all 21 strikes (-387 at 950 through -3,817 at 1150), so no gamma flip exists and dealers still hedge with the move at every quoted level.

+9.2 points on the future to 1013.3 came with 1040-call IV falling 15.43 to 13.33 and 1050-call IV 15.35 to 13.28 (-2.1 each), while 980-put IV rose 13.14 to 13.50: the entire IV compression was an upside-call crush, not a broad de-rating.

624 contracts traded the 1070 call yet its OI fell 1,188 to 997 (-191) and its IV dropped 15.04 to 12.87 — volume without OI build is closing flow (Vol2Vol), so the upside wing was sold into strength rather than bought.

13.13% ATM IV is the 89th percentile of this series' 38-session history (10.57-14.27, median 11.82) but is down 1.05 points in a day, with put OI -164 and put volume collapsing to 1,112 (P/C volume 0.49 from 1.50).

S50Z26.today_summary: 1013.3 on the Dec future, +9.2, with 48 days to the 2026-12-29 expiry and max pain 16.7 points above at 1030. Net GEX stayed negative at every one of the 21 strikes (-3,817 total) but its magnitude halved from -7,476, because the public closed its 1070 call wing — 624 contracts traded against a 191-lot OI drawdown and a 2.17-point IV collapse at that strike. Per-strike net GEX turns positive at 1030 (+446) and builds to +1,444 at 1050, so the 1030-1060 shelf is a dampening zone while everything below 1013 is still amplified air. The posture the structure supports is reduce and stand aside: the force that drove the last two weeks is being dismantled, not replaced.
what_changed: Upside call IV collapsed 2.1 points (1040C 15.43 to 13.33, 1050C 15.35 to 13.28) on a 9.2-point rally — the opposite of what a fresh upside bid looks like.
Short-gamma burden halved to -3,817 net GEX from -7,476, and -4,143 from -6,396 in the 990-1030 ATM band, as dealers bought back gamma against the closed 1070 calls.
25D skew swung +1.75 to +0.17 (980P 13.50 vs 1040C 13.33), erasing yesterday's -1.58 call-side richness and leaving the index with no protection bid at all.
The 960 put wall (3,056 OI) fell outside the +/-5% active band as the future rallied, promoting 1000 (2,088 OI, 273 contracts — the strip's heaviest put volume) to live support.
S50Z26.five_day_thesis: Five sessions ago on 2026-11-04 the future was 1017.9 with max pain 1040, 29,564 total OI and -7,893 net GEX; the 11-07 break to 991.3 spiked IV to 14.27, added 3,971 OI in a day and pushed 25D skew put-rich to +0.9 as protection was bought. Everything since has been the reversal of that trade: the future recovered 22.0 points to 1013.3, IV faded to 13.13, total OI bled 35,408 to 34,501, and skew round-tripped to flat +0.17. Call OI grew 27.8% over the window (15,014 to 19,181) but the growth is stale structure — the 1100 strike holds 2,824 contracts on 66 lots of volume while the live flow at 1070 is closing. Max pain drifted down 10 points to 1030 and the 1100 call / 960 put walls have not moved in eight sessions, so the chain's skeleton is unchanged while its energy drains. The highest-signal fact is that short gamma has compressed 52% from -7,893 to -3,817 without ever crossing zero: the amplifier is weakening but not gone, so a break still gets helped along rather than absorbed.

strategies.name: Iron condor 960/980 put x 1050/1070 call
strategies.rationale: 13.13% IV sits at the 89th percentile of 38 sessions while both wings bleed OI (put OI -164, 1070 calls -191 on 624 closing lots), so this sells elevated vol into a structure losing its driver; the short strikes are the 25D band edges (980/1040 per delta_bands, taken out to 1050 at the 2,004-OI near call wall) and sit 33.3 and 36.7 points away versus an 8.38-point 1-sigma day.
strategies.defined_risk: Max loss = 20-point wing width minus net credit, one side only — 20 points equals 4,000 baht per contract at the 200-baht multiplier, before credit. Must be sized small: with net GEX negative at all 21 strikes, dealers amplify any break rather than absorb it, and the 25D short strikes carry roughly a 25% chance each of finishing in the money.
strategies.invalidation: A close below 1000 (2,088 put OI, the live support) or above 1050 (2,004 OI near call wall). This is a vega trade on IV reverting toward the 11.82 median, not a pin bet — 48 DTE is far too long for pinning mechanics.

strategies.name: Bull call debit spread 1020/1050
strategies.rationale: The 2.1-point upside-call IV crush makes this the cheapest the 1020-1050 structure has been in vol terms since 11-06, and it targets the 1030 max-pain hinge where per-strike net GEX turns positive (+446 at 1030, +1,444 at 1050) — a dampening shelf that favours a grind into the strikes rather than a run through them.
strategies.defined_risk: Max loss = net debit paid, capped by the 30-point width (6,000 baht per contract at 200 baht per point). Low conviction: the public just closed this wing, so the position is buying what better-informed flow sold.
strategies.invalidation: A close below 1000 — below the live put support the strip has no positive-gamma support until 1030, and short-gamma hedging works against the long-call leg.

strategies.name: Put debit spread 1000/970 (hedge overlay)
strategies.rationale: With cumulative net GEX negative at all 21 strikes and no gamma flip anywhere in the chain, a break of 1000 is hedged with the move by dealers, so the air pocket below the live support is the one genuinely amplified path; 980-put IV at 13.50 is 1.02 points below its 11-07 level of 14.52 despite the protection bid having been fully paid down.
strategies.defined_risk: Max loss = net debit paid, capped by the 30-point width (6,000 baht per contract). Mutually exclusive with the condor above, which sells the downside wing this buys — they are alternative expressions, not a combined book.
strategies.invalidation: A close above 1030 (max pain and the strike where per-strike net GEX turns positive) — above it dealer hedging dampens rather than accelerates, and the amplification premise is gone.

S50Z26.prediction: 1013.3 to 1030 is the path of least resistance: max pain sits at 1030 and per-strike net GEX turns positive there, so drift up into the 1030-1050 dampening shelf is the structurally favoured outcome, with the 8.38-point 1-sigma day implying roughly two sessions to cover the 16.7-point gap. Conviction is low and the vol signal outranks the directional one — the public closed its upside calls into this rally, which argues for a grind rather than continuation. A close below 1000 invalidates it outright: with no gamma flip in the chain, dealers amplify downside from there toward the 960 structural floor.
S50Z26.risk_note: Educational analysis only — not trade advice, and nothing here recommends executing a trade. SET50 options are European and cash-settled on the SET50 index, so there is no physical delivery and the dealer-hedging mechanics behind pinning are structurally weaker than for single stocks that settle in shares: treat max pain at 1030 as a tendency and an anchor, not a target or a guarantee. At 48 DTE pinning is not in play at all. Defined-risk is not risk-free — the capped max loss on every structure above is real and does occur, short-vol payoffs are negative-skew (small frequent gains, rare large losses), and survival depends on position size rather than forecast accuracy. Macro and news flow can override the entire option structure, and the 1100 call wall (2,824 OI on 66 lots of volume) is stale structure that should not be weighted as live resistance.
